articles.title: Nifty crosses 23,800 for first time since August on falling crude prices, earnings boost
articles.excerpt:
Markets closed higher for the fourth straight session on Tuesday, with the Nifty crossing the 23,800 mark for the first time since August 2026, as falling crude oil prices, strong corporate earnings and returning foreign investors combined to sustain the rally. The Sensex closed at 76,918, up 1,225 points or 1.62 per cent, while the Nifty settled at 23,810.85, up 370 points or 1.58 per cent.

Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services, noted that “easing crude oil prices, alongside hopes of de-escalation in West Asia following progress in Iran-Qatar discussions, are supporting sentiment,” adding that the Nifty Capital Markets index surged 4.5 per cent on the day.

articles.title: Indian gold demand down 30% in September quarter as high prices hurt jewellery sales
articles.excerpt:
Gold demand in the September quarter plunged 30 per cent to 162 tonnes against 230 tonnes. | Photo Credit: RUPAK DE CHOWDHURI

Gold demand in India during the September quarter plunged 30 per cent to 162 tonnes against 230 tonnes logged in the same period last year as the high prices pulled down jewellery sales.

In value terms, the gold demand was up 3 per cent at ₹2.42 lakh crore (₹2.35 lakh crore), largely due to rupee depreciation against dollar, according to the World Gold Council data released on Tuesday.
